purpose: Independent, filing-reconciled ownership map and enterprise-to-equity valuation bridge for the 2026-Q2 information set.

primary_sources.ref: TEQ.ST/official-reports/interim-reports/2026/2026-07-18 - Interim Report April - June 2026 - Teqnion AB.pdf
locators: page 21: acquisition-payment liabilities at fair value
pages 23-24: acquisition accounting and segment EBITA
page 57: liquidity and contractual-liability maturity table
page 58: net-debt/EBITDA target and capital-allocation policy
page 61: 2025 acquisition consideration and acquired earnings
page 67: 55,500 warrants at 265.11 SEK exercise price

component_ownership_map.label: 100% of the owned operating-company portfolio
component_ownership_map.scope: R12 enterprise cash flow from subsidiaries already owned at 2026-06-30. Future acquisitions and their purchase prices are both excluded.

component_ownership_map.label: Cash less bank debt, leases, acquisition-payment liabilities, and non-controlling interest
component_ownership_map.scope: All reported financing claims are deducted at carrying value; unused credit capacity is not an equity asset.

non_double_counting_rules: The current operating portfolio is valued once on enterprise cash flow; cash and every financing claim are then bridged once to parent equity.

Acquisition cash payments are excluded only because benefits from future, unannounced acquisitions are also excluded. Completed acquisitions are already represented by consolidated R12 cash flow and outstanding acquisition-payment liabilities.
The 182.8 MSEK of other financial liabilities is deducted at the reported fair value/probable outcome; it is not probability-discounted again.
The unused revolving facility is financing capacity, not cash or intrinsic value.
First North liquidity and execution risk affect discount rates and terminal multiples; no reserve tied to market price is subtracted from intrinsic value.
The 55,500 warrants at 265.11 SEK are out of the money in all three cases and are excluded from current diluted shares under the issuer's Q2 presentation; they remain a monitored dilution item.

gap_assessments.reconciliation: Two additive components cover the operating enterprise and its complete financing/equity bridge with unique overlap keys.
gap_assessments.remaining_uncertainty: No value is assigned to unannounced acquisitions; this is deliberate rather than missing scope.
gap_assessments.falsifier: A material off-balance-sheet claim or a separately owned asset not represented in consolidated cash flow is identified.
gap_assessments.monitoring_source: Quarterly balance sheet, cash-flow statement, acquisition notes, and share-count note.

gap_assessments.reconciliation: The proof reproduces R12 FCF ex acquisitions as 213.5 - 8.6 = 204.9 MSEK, converts it to enterprise cash flow with after-tax cash financing cost, and discounts causal low/base/high schedules.
gap_assessments.remaining_uncertainty: Working-capital timing and record R12 margins drive the 85%-100% starting normalization range.
gap_assessments.falsifier: R12 cash flow falls below 85% of the 2026-Q2 run rate without a temporary working-capital explanation, organic decline persists, or EBITA margin falls below 9%.
gap_assessments.monitoring_source: Quarterly income statement, segment note, and cash-flow statement.

gap_assessments.reconciliation: 552.5 MSEK bank debt, 163.5 MSEK leases, 182.8 MSEK fair-valued acquisition-payment liabilities, and 1.4 MSEK minority interest are deducted; 171.5 MSEK cash is added.
gap_assessments.remaining_uncertainty: Earnout fair values can be remeasured and new acquisitions can change the capital structure after the report date.
gap_assessments.falsifier: Net debt/EBITDA approaches 2.5x, acquisition-payment liabilities rise faster than acquired cash earnings, or material dilution is issued below intrinsic value.
gap_assessments.monitoring_source: Quarterly liquidity table, financial-instrument note, acquisition note, and share-count note.

committee_conclusion: The model is stock-specific and evidence-clear enough for independent committee review. It is not a human capital decision.
